statement.text:
Does there exist a class X of finite groups satisfying the following conditions:
   (1) X is closed with respect to taking subgroups and homomorphic images;
   (2) the product of two normal X-subgroups of an arbitrary group is always an
X-group;
   (3) for every positive integer n, there exist a finite group and its conjugacy class
D such that any n elements of D generate an X-subgroup, whereas ⟨D⟩ ∈      / X.
    It is known that there are no classes X satisfying (1)–(3) that are closed with
respect to extensions (D. O. Revin, Algebra i Analiz, 37, no. 1 (2025), 141–176 (Rus-
sian)).                                                                     D. O. Revin
